decisions.reason: The 518 FLEX is a rebranded upgrade of the established BASIC 518, which the website says has already won many friends, so it meets the aspiration and gives no reason for problemistic search.
The flail shredders get a dedicated page, which signals active commitment, and with no reported shortfall the established firm's slack lets it keep them while results build.
The grinder is only mentioned and its results are uncertain, but one year is too early to judge it against aspirations, so the firm carries it within its broad shredding range.
The stationary electric fine shredder has only a weak web presence and no performance evidence, yet without a clear shortfall management tolerates it while it matures.

The green-waste grinder overlaps with Product C and is only mentioned, which makes it the most likely candidate for consolidation, but there is no evidence yet of a shortfall that would trigger dropping it.
The single-shaft pre-shredders have their own page and fit the firm's core stationary waste-processing business, so they are likely kept.
